schema.description: Leaving home on a trip, one row in a records file (source records), written from itineraries, bookings and emails. Opens a travel.trip series; values are the row's own text.

agency.description: The travel agent the trip was booked through, with its reference where the source gave one, as written.

basis.description: The evidence the row rests on, free text as the extraction wrote it: a booking, an email, or a note that the date is inferred. Read it before trusting the date.

booking.description: The booking reference (airline record locator or agent's code) as written.

date.description: The day of departure. Sydney local date, YYYY-MM-DD, as the records row writes it. This is the fact time.

destination.description: Where the trip went, free text as written: one place, a country, or a list.

from.description: The city the trip left from, as written.

id.description: The row id the records file assigns, chosen once. The travel history writes it as <origin>:<trip>/<kind>, with the date and a place or route appended where a trip has several rows of a kind. This is the identity.

purpose.description: Why the trip was made, free text as written.

trip.description: The trip key every row of one trip shares (departed, arrived, returned, flight), written by the extraction as the year and month of departure and a short slug. It names the travel.trip series. travel.returned with the same key closes it.
